original_question: In the boundary case where p is the smallest prime divisor of n and p = hm - h + 1, classify all m-element subsets A of a finite abelian group G for which the h-fold sumset hA has minimum possible size. In particular, beyond arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p, determine all subsets that can occur in this extremal case.
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the unlabelled open inverse problem stated immediately after Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: after Proposition 1.2 identifies the minimum value in the regime m ≤ p and Theorem 1.3 handles the strict inequality hm - h + 1 < p, the paper singles out the remaining boundary case p = hm - h + 1 and asks for a classification of all extremal m-subsets A with minimum h-fold sumset. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient setting of finite abelian groups, the boundary regime p = hm - h + 1 with p the smallest prime divisor of n, the inverse-problem nature of the question, and the two model families explicitly mentioned in the paper: arithmetic progressions of length m and m-subsets contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p. That is exactly the leftover case isolated after Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
missing_details: You should explicitly state that G has order n and that p is the smallest prime divisor of n.
You should include the standing hypothesis m ≤ p; this is part of the special-case setup supplied by Proposition 1.2 and used in the surrounding discussion.
You should define the h-fold sumset as hA = {a1 + ··· + ah : a1,...,ah ∈ A}.
You should state the extremal condition as |hA| = ρ(G,m,h), where ρ(G,m,h) = min{|hB| : B ⊆ G, |B| = m}.
Because this is the boundary case p = hm - h + 1, Proposition 1.2 makes the minimum explicit: ρ(G,m,h) = p. Writing this out makes the question stand alone.
To match the paper’s nontrivial intent, you should exclude the trivial case h = 1 (or note separately that then every m-subset is extremal).
You should clarify that a 'subset contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p' means A ⊆ a + H for some subgroup H ≤ G with |H| = p.
You should make clear that the question is not to prove Conjecture 1.1 or reprove Theorem 1.3, but to classify the remaining extremal sets in the exact boundary case left open immediately after them.
refined_question: Let G be a finite abelian group of order n, let p be the smallest prime divisor of n, and let m and h be positive integers with h ≥ 2, m ≤ p, and p = hm - h + 1. For an m-subset A ⊆ G, define hA = {a1 + ··· + ah : a1,...,ah ∈ A} and ρ(G,m,h) = min{|hB| : B ⊆ G, |B| = m}. Since Proposition 1.2 gives ρ(G,m,h) = p in this boundary case, classify all m-subsets A ⊆ G for which |hA| = ρ(G,m,h) = p; equivalently, determine all extremal sets in this remaining case, not only the known examples consisting of arithmetic progressions of length m and subsets contained in a coset a + H of a subgroup H ≤ G with |H| = p.
equivalent_formulation: Under the same hypotheses, classify all m-subsets A ⊆ G such that |hA| = p. This is equivalent to the refined question because Proposition 1.2 shows that when m ≤ p and p = hm - h + 1, one has ρ(G,m,h) = min{p, hm - h + 1} = p. ([static.uni-graz.at](https://static.uni-graz.at/fileadmin/veranstaltungen/additive2016/Talks/bajnok_b_slides.pdf))
justification: Conjecture 1.1 treats the regime m ≤ p < hm - h + 1 and predicts that the only extremal sets are those contained in a coset of a subgroup of order p; Theorem 1.3 treats hm - h + 1 < p and gives arithmetic progressions as the extremal sets; Proposition 1.2 supplies the special-case minimum ρ(G,m,h) = min{p, hm - h + 1} when m ≤ p. Immediately after this trio of statements, the paper explicitly says that the remaining case p = hm - h + 1 has several possibilities and that it would be interesting to classify all such subsets. That is exactly the research question your draft is reaching for, and the rewrite above sharpens it without broadening it beyond the paper’s stated intent. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1512.03038))
